71:         Measure.
72:         In EMNLP-CoNLL (Vol. 7, pp. 410-420).
73: """
74: 
75: import collections
76: import warnings
77: 
78: import numpy as np
79: import scipy.stats
80: import scipy.sparse
81: import scipy.special
82: 
83: from . import util
84: 
85: 
86: def validate_boundary(reference_intervals, estimated_intervals, trim):
87:     """Check that the input annotations to a segment boundary estimation
88:     metric (i.e. one that only takes in segment intervals) look like valid
89:     segment times, and throws helpful errors if not.
90: 
91:     Parameters
92:     ----------
93:     reference_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
94:         reference segment intervals, in the format returned by
95:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
96:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
97:     estimated_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m, 2)
98:         estimated segment intervals, in the format returned by
99:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
100:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
101:     trim : bool
102:         will the start and end events be trimmed?
103:     """
104:     if trim:
105:         # If we're trimming, then we need at least 2 intervals
106:         min_size = 2
107:     else:
108:         # If we're not trimming, then we only need one interval
109:         min_size = 1
110: 
111:     if len(reference_intervals) < min_size:
112:         warnings.warn("Reference intervals are empty.")
113: 
114:     if len(estimated_intervals) < min_size:
115:         warnings.warn("Estimated intervals are empty.")
116: 
117:     for intervals in [reference_intervals, estimated_intervals]:
118:         util.validate_intervals(intervals)
119: 
120: 
121: def validate_structure(
122:     reference_intervals, reference_labels, estimated_intervals, estimated_labels
123: ):
124:     """Check that the input annotations to a structure estimation metric (i.e.
125:     one that takes in both segment boundaries and their labels) look like valid
126:     segment times and labels, and throws helpful errors if not.
127: 
128:     Parameters
129:     ----------
130:     reference_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
131:         reference segment intervals, in the format returned by
132:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
133:     reference_labels : list, shape=(n,)
134:         reference segment labels, in the format returned by
135:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
136:     estimated_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m, 2)
137:         estimated segment intervals, in the format returned by
138:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
139:     estimated_labels : list, shape=(m,)
140:         estimated segment labels, in the format returned by
141:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
142: 
143:     """
144:     for intervals, labels in [
145:         (reference_intervals, reference_labels),
146:         (estimated_intervals, estimated_labels),
147:     ]:
148:         util.validate_intervals(intervals)
149:         if intervals.shape[0] != len(labels):
150:             raise ValueError("Number of intervals does not match number " "of labels")
151: 
152:         # Check only when intervals are non-empty
153:         if intervals.size > 0:
154:             # Make sure intervals start at 0
155:             if not np.allclose(intervals.min(), 0.0):
156:                 raise ValueError("Segment intervals do not start at 0")
157: 
158:     if reference_intervals.size == 0:
159:         warnings.warn("Reference intervals are empty.")
160:     if estimated_intervals.size == 0:
161:         warnings.warn("Estimated intervals are empty.")
162:     # Check only when intervals are non-empty
163:     if reference_intervals.size > 0 and estimated_intervals.size > 0:
164:         if not np.allclose(reference_intervals.max(), estimated_intervals.max()):
165:             raise ValueError("End times do not match")
166: 
167: 
168: def detection(
169:     reference_intervals, estimated_intervals, window=0.5, beta=1.0, trim=False
170: ):
171:     """Boundary detection hit-rate.
172: 
173:     A hit is counted whenever an reference boundary is within ``window`` of a
174:     estimated boundary.  Note that each boundary is matched at most once: this
175:     is achieved by computing the size of a maximal matching between reference
176:     and estimated boundary points, subject to the window constraint.
177: 
178:     Examples
179:     --------
180:     >>> ref_intervals, _ = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('ref.lab')
181:     >>> est_intervals, _ = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('est.lab')
182:     >>> # With 0.5s windowing
183:     >>> P05, R05, F05 = mir_eval.segment.detection(ref_intervals,
184:     ...                                            est_intervals,
185:     ...                                            window=0.5)
186:     >>> # With 3s windowing
187:     >>> P3, R3, F3 = mir_eval.segment.detection(ref_intervals,
188:     ...                                         est_intervals,
189:     ...                                         window=3)
190:     >>> # Ignoring hits for the beginning and end of track
191:     >>> P, R, F = mir_eval.segment.detection(ref_intervals,
192:     ...                                      est_intervals,
193:     ...                                      window=0.5,
194:     ...                                      trim=True)
195: 
196:     Parameters
197:     ----------
198:     reference_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
199:         reference segment intervals, in the format returned by
200:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
201:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
202:     estimated_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m, 2)
203:         estimated segment intervals, in the format returned by
204:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
205:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
206:     window : float > 0
207:         size of the window of 'correctness' around ground-truth beats
208:         (in seconds)
209:         (Default value = 0.5)
210:     beta : float > 0
211:         weighting constant for F-measure.
212:         (Default value = 1.0)
213:     trim : boolean
214:         if ``True``, the first and last boundary times are ignored.
215:         Typically, these denote start (0) and end-markers.
216:         (Default value = False)
217: 
218:     Returns
219:     -------
220:     precision : float
221:         precision of estimated predictions
222:     recall : float
223:         recall of reference reference boundaries
224:     f_measure : float
225:         F-measure (weighted harmonic mean of ``precision`` and ``recall``)
226:     """
